transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-29 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Megan (Redwood PM), Kari (Sparrow Head of Alliances), Samir (Sparrow AE), Riley (Sparrow SA)
---
[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda — we want to align on Acme, hand off the co-sell plan, and make sure the technical checklist for the pilot is clear.
[00:18] Kari: Yep thanks Alex, excited. we had a good intro with Acme last week, they want faster gen latency and tighter data residency. they'll be picky on KMS and audit logs.
[00:34] Samir: to add, their timeline is aggressive, decisioning in 6–8 weeks. budget is flexible if we can show throughput at scale and consistent latency.
[00:48] Priya: cool, so technical question first — Acme cares about inference latency at 95th percentiles sub-200ms on short prompts, and about embedding throughput for similarity search. we should confirm sequence lengths and expected QPS.
[01:05] Riley: sorry, quick interrupt — their current stack is a mix: user-facing features on CloudGiant endpoints, and an on-prem data layer. they won't ship PII off-shore. so VPC or on-prem Private deployment is likely table stakes.
[01:22] Alex: noted. from Redwood side, we can propose Dedicated pool in the region for predictable throughput, or Private VPC if they need full network isolation. difference in cost probably 20–40% more for Private, roughly.
[01:38] Kari: can you remind us on compliance? they asked specifically for KMS integration and audit logs for model inputs/outputs retention policy. also SSO — SAML.
[01:50] Megan: yes, Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS, HSM integrations, and we provide audit logs with configurable retention. we have SOC 2 Type II reports — I'll attach the security pack.
[02:04] Samir: will your audit logs include token-level traces or just high-level request logs?
[02:11] Priya: we can provide token-level cost and latency breakdown per request if needed, but for security we can redact content and provide metadata. depends on the retention policy Acme wants.
[02:26] Riley: good. they also asked about fallback behavior; how would you handle a Dedicated outage?
[02:33] Alex: auto-fallback to a hosted model variant in another region is possible — policy-based routing. there is an SLA delta though. we can put a canary route so critical latency requests hit Dedicated and non-critical use cases can go to hosted.
[02:50] Kari: pricing is going to be a sticking point. we want partner-friendly rates so Sparrow can co-sell and still take a margin. can we get a partner discount slab?
[02:59] Megan: yes. typical partner co-sell discounts are in tiers — e.g., 10% for up to X committed spend, 15% above that, plus possible reseller margins. Alex will pull a proposal.
[03:12] Samir: also need clarity on lead attribution and procurement flow — who finalizes the contract? Sparrow or Redwood?
[03:20] Alex: proposal tends to be joint — Redwood quotes and legal goes through Acme, but Sparrow can be the selling party on the SOW. we'll define referral vs reseller motion in the partnership doc.
[03:34] Riley: technical deep-dive — on the benchmarking: what metrics will you measure?
[03:40] Priya: we'll measure p50/p95 latency for generation, max sustainable QPS for embeddings, GPU utilization, and token cost per call. also we will look at warm-up KV cache behavior — I sometimes see people call it K V cache — and how it affects cold starts.
[03:59] Samir: will you need sample payloads? Acme's prompts include multi-turn chat with ~600 tokens and semantics ranker calls for search.
[04:10] Priya: please share representative prompt sets. We'll draft a bench plan that includes 1) short prompts (<=64 tokens), 2) medium chat (300–700 tokens), 3) batch embedding run (10k vectors) to emulate reindexing.
[04:30] Alex: timeline: if Priya runs the benchmark within two weeks we can have data for Acme exec review before their decision window.
[04:38] Kari: perfect. one more thing — legal asked about data residency controls and proof of deletion. do you have APIs for purge requests?
[04:47] Megan: yes we provide deletion endpoints and can include contractual language for deletion windows and audit logs. we'll share the compliance doc.
[04:55] Riley: on networking, Acme requires IP allowlisting and private peering. do you support private peering to our VPC?
[05:02] Alex: yes, Redwood Private supports VPC peering and we can set up static IPs for allowlisting. setup lead time depends on their networking team but estimate 2–4 weeks.
[05:12] Samir: competition — they are also talking to VectraAI and the incumbent CloudGiant offering. CloudGiant is cheaper for hosted but lacks the Dedicated peering options.
[05:23] Priya: okay moving to success criteria: what would Acme need to sign?
[05:27] Kari: 1) p95 latency <= 200ms for short prompts; 2) embedding throughput >= 2k QPS for similarity API; 3) contractual KMS and audit logs; 4) partner-friendly commercial terms.
[05:40] Alex: agreed. we'll aim the proposal at hitting those four buckets.
[05:45] Riley: any concerns about model fidelity or hallucination for their domain? they have internal taxonomies and strong regulatory wording — hallucination tolerance is low.
[05:56] Priya: we'll include prompt templates and evaluation harness to monitor quality and regressions. Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization and model variants to keep cost down while preserving quality. sometimes the transcriber shows that as Redwood Opti-mize — hope that wasn't confusing.
[06:16] Samir: great. back to pricing: can you sketch a sample for Dedicated vs Hosted with partner margin?
[06:23] Alex: high level: Hosted: pay-as-you-go, no commitment, unit cost higher; Dedicated: committed monthly capacity with lower per-token and embedding unit costs; Private: Dedicated + network isolation + KMS, premium on top. we'll send concrete numbers in the deck.
[06:40] Kari: ok we need a co-sell one-pager for Acme execs — short, bulletized success criteria and a single slide on cost/latency tradeoffs.
[06:48] Megan: we'll create that and include a technical appendix. I'll also attach SOC2 and KMS integration notes.
[06:57] Alex: let's align on the benchmark plan's acceptance criteria: p95 latency under 200ms for short prompts, embedding batch throughput sustained at our target for >5 minutes without degradation, and a plan to replay 10k sample queries. Priya will own the run.
[07:13] Priya: will do. I'll also capture GPU types and quantization settings in the test plan.
[07:20] Riley: FYI Acme's legal prefers a 90-day data retention and ability to request deletion within 7 days notice.
[07:28] Megan: we can propose a 45-day default retention with contractual option — we'll flag that as negotiable.
[07:35] Samir: are there any blockers on Redwood's side for a pilot starting within two weeks?
[07:40] Alex: only dependency is getting sample prompts/data and agreement on QPS targets. otherwise Redwood can provision a Dedicated pool quickly if the contract or commitment is OK.
[07:50] Kari: awesome. sounds good.
[07:53] Alex: quick recap of next steps: Alex to send co-sell proposal & one-pager; Megan to share security pack; Priya to draft benchmark plan; Kari to provide Acme contacts and sample prompts; schedule exec intro.
[08:06] Riley: can you also append contact matrix (who owns legal, procurement, security)? I'll pull that together.
[08:11] Alex: perfect. any other questions before we wrap?
[08:15] Samir: none from me.
[08:17] Priya: none, we'll sync after initial benchmark run.
[08:21] Megan: I'll draft the partner pricing slab and include an example math for margins, send by June 2.
[08:30] Alex: thanks everyone. end of call.
---
Notes: occasional transcription artifacts: "K V cache" wrote as K-V cache; Redwood Optimize sometimes transcribed as Redwood Opti-mize; minor name mislabels in the auto-attribution.
